history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. 'Nagaland Christian Revival Church' is a generic denomination name, not a single identifiable church. The Nagaland Christian Revival Church denomination was formed in 1961 out of the Naga revival movement of the 1950s-1970s (second wave September 1976), when traditional Baptist churches rejected the revival and thousands joined the new denomination. Multiple map listings under this name exist across Nagaland (Chumukedima, Dimapur, Changtongya, Kohima, Mokokchung-Alichen). The closest Zunheboto-addressed referent found is a listing titled 'Nagaland Christian Revival Church, Mishilimi' with address 'Zunheboto, Nagaland, IN' at 25.882867, 94.259884; it is unclear whether this is the congregation the CSV intends. Coordinates, founding details and visiting information are therefore provisional. Flag for Mahesh: either pin this record to a confirmed local congregation or drop it.

town_description: Zunheboto (also Zünhebo, 'Land of Warriors') is a town in Zunheboto district, Nagaland, at about 1,852 m elevation, with a 2011 population of 22,809. It is inhabited by the Sumi Nagas; the district is 97.3% Christian. The name comes from the zünhebo flowering shrub (Leucosceptrum) abundant on the hill tops where the town is built.

travel.airport: Nearest airport: Dimapur Airport (verify distance, about 200 km by road).
travel.road: Connected by road from Kohima and Mokokchung via NH and state highways.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for cool, clear weather; December (Christmas season) is the most festive but crowded time. An Inner Line Permit is required for visitors from other Indian states.
